candidates.workingClaim: September 25, 1957: On September 25, 1957, federal troops escorted the Little Rock Nine into Central High School for their first full day of classes. The students had faced violent opposition to desegregation. Federal protection made attendance possible, but did not end the hostility they experienced.
September 25, 1066: On September 25, 1066, King Harold's forces defeated Harald Hardrada at Stamford Bridge. Hardrada was killed. Harold soon faced another invasion in southern England.

September 25, 1789: On September 25, 1789, the First Congress proposed twelve amendments to the U.S. Constitution. Ten were ratified in 1791 and became the Bill of Rights; another was ratified more than two centuries later as the Twenty-Seventh Amendment.

September 25, 1992: On September 25, 1992, NASA launched Mars Observer to study the planet's surface, atmosphere, and interior from orbit. Contact with the spacecraft was lost in 1993, shortly before its planned arrival at Mars.

September 26, 2022: On September 26, 2022, NASA's DART spacecraft struck Dimorphos, the small companion of asteroid Didymos. The experiment tested whether a spacecraft impact could change an asteroid's motion; this asteroid system was not threatening Earth.

September 26, 1907: On September 26, 1907, Prime Minister Joseph Ward proclaimed New Zealand's dominion status. It was a change within the British Empire, not a single declaration of complete independence.

September 26, 1580: On September 26, 1580, Francis Drake returned to Plymouth in the Golden Hind after circling the globe. His voyage was the first English circumnavigation, but it also formed part of an era of English privateering, colonial expansion, and the transatlantic slave trade.

September 26, 1960: On September 26, 1960, John F. Kennedy and Richard Nixon met in Chicago for the first televised debate between U.S. presidential candidates. It was the first of four debates between the candidates during that campaign.

September 27, 1825: On September 27, 1825, George Stephenson drove Locomotion No. 1 at the opening of the Stockton and Darlington Railway. The event became a landmark in the development of public steam rail transport.

September 27, 1822: On September 27, 1822, Jean-Francois Champollion presented his research in the Letter to M. Dacier. Building on earlier scholarship, his method helped make ancient Egyptian texts readable again.

September 27, 1540: On September 27, 1540, Pope Paul III promulgated the bull Regimini Militantis Ecclesiae, recognizing the Society of Jesus as a religious order. The order was founded around Ignatius of Loyola and would become widely known as the Jesuits.

September 27, 1940: On September 27, 1940, Germany, Italy, and Japan signed the Tripartite Pact in Berlin. The agreement pledged cooperation among the Axis powers and threatened support for any power entering the war against them outside Europe or Asia.
September 28, 1066: On September 28, 1066, William's fleet reached Pevensey in Sussex. The landing opened the invasion that led to the Battle of Hastings in October.

September 28, 1924: On September 28, 1924, the U.S. Army Air Service's round-the-world expedition concluded. Erik Nelson, piloting New Orleans, was among those who completed the pioneering journey that began in April.

September 28, 1542: On September 28, 1542, the vessels led by Juan Rodriguez Cabrillo entered what is now San Diego Bay. The expedition made contact with the Kumeyaay, who were already living in the region; the Spanish named the bay Puerto de San Miguel.

September 28, 1781: On September 28, 1781, American and French forces marched from Williamsburg to Yorktown and began investing the British positions. Their operation would culminate in the British surrender under Lord Cornwallis the following month.
September 29, 1954: On September 29, 1954, the CERN Convention entered into force after the necessary ratifications. The organization created a shared framework for research in fundamental physics.

September 29, 1988: On September 29, 1988, Discovery launched on mission STS-26. It was the Space Shuttle program's return to flight after the 1986 Challenger disaster, following extensive technical and organizational changes.
September 29, 1979: On September 29, 1979, Pope John Paul II arrived in Ireland and addressed President Patrick Hillery in Dublin. His pastoral visit continued into October.

September 29, 1941: On September 29, 1941, SS and German police units and their auxiliaries began the mass murder of Kyiv's Jews at the Babyn Yar ravine. The mass shooting continued the next day and became one of the largest massacres of the Holocaust.
September 30, 1966: On September 30, 1966, Botswana became independent from Britain with Seretse Khama as its first president. The new republic replaced the Bechuanaland Protectorate.

September 30, 2016: On September 30, 2016, ESA's Rosetta spacecraft ended its mission with a controlled impact on comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko. It transmitted observations during descent before communication ceased.

September 30, 1949: On September 30, 1949, the U.S. Air Force made its final Berlin Airlift flight from Rhein-Main Air Base. The Soviet blockade had been lifted in May; British flights continued until October 6.

September 30, 1938: Over the night of September 29-30, 1938, Germany, Italy, Great Britain, and France signed the Munich Agreement. Czechoslovakia, which was not a party to the negotiations, was forced to surrender its Sudeten border regions and defenses to Nazi Germany.

October 1, 1958: On October 1, 1958, the National Aeronautics and Space Administration officially began operations. NASA incorporated the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics and assumed leadership of the United States' civilian space program.
October 1, 1960: On October 1, 1960, Nigeria gained independence from Britain. The new country adopted a federal constitutional system, with Abubakar Tafawa Balewa serving as prime minister.
October 1, 1949: On October 1, 1949, Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the Central People's Government of the People's Republic of China from Tiananmen Gate in Beijing.
October 1, 1978: On October 1, 1978, Tuvalu became independent. The Constitution of Tuvalu defines Independence Day as October 1, 1978.
